newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Montenegrin leader expresses concern over crisis.
newsitem.headline: Montenegrin leader expresses concern over crisis.

text.p: A Montenegrin politician has delivered indirect criticism of his socialist allies in Serbia over the handling of a crisis set off by alleged poll fraud, Montenegrin media reported.
Svetozar Marovic, speaker of the Montenegrin republic parliament, called on Serbian authorities to respect the democratic process, the Montena-Fax news agency reported.
"No one has the right to change the foundation of democracy -- the will of the people -- regardless of whether it's done by the authorities or by the opposition," he was quoted as saying.
Marovic, a member of Montenegro's Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS), also appeared to warn against a possible police crackdown after two weeks of opposition street protests.
"It is very important in the most difficult of situations that those who take care of the people and the state keep a cool and rational head," he said.
His critical comments came as Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic was confronted with a wave of demonstrations that have caused him damage at home and abroad.
Milosevic dominates Serbia and its junior partner in the Yugoslav federation, Montenegro.
An opposition coalition has led street protests in Belgrade and other major towns in Serbia after authorities annulled an opposition victory in municipal polls in Belgrade and elsewhere.

"I believe a democratic solution will be found in Serbia for overcoming the current situation and that which was the will of the people, without any so to speak -- administrative intervention -- will be the foundation of local, republican and federal authority," Marovic said.
He also referred to a debate in Montenegro about Milosevic's possible candidacy for Yugoslav president.
Milosevic's candidacy was seen by some as "the only solution and by others as the personification of concentration of too much power in one person".
